sense: have to: it has to be done

terms.gloss: it must be done; I must do it
terms.grammar: the gerundive with sum; the person who must, in the dative
evidence: Ter. Ph. 318: tibi omne est exedendum
terms.comment: The commonest way to say “must” and “have to”. Without an object it stands in the neuter (edendum est, I have to eat); with one, it agrees with it (tantum nivis fodiendum fuit, so much snow had to be dug).

terms.gloss: it is necessary, it has to be
terms.grammar: phrase, with an infinitive, an accusative and infinitive, or a bare subjunctive
evidence: Publil. Sent. N 32: Necesse est maximōrum minima esse initia.
terms.comment: What cannot be otherwise: necessity, not duty (see necessary).
Of what is required or fitting (see should); with a bare subjunctive, discās oportet, you must learn.

terms.grammar: phrase, with a dative of the person and an infinitive
terms.comment: “Mustn’t” of a rule (see allow); said to someone as an order, nōlī with the infinitive (see don’t!). Nōn necesse est is “needn’t”.

evidence: Varr. RR 1.1.2: rogās, ut id mihi habeam cūrāre (Lewis & Short s.v. habeō)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to have or be obliged to do something”, ante-classical and post-Augustan. Classically habeō dīcere is “I have something to say, I can say” (see say); for “must”, faciendum est (above).

phrases.latin: Tūte hoc intrīstī: tibi omne est exedendum.
phrases.english: You cooked this up yourself: you have to eat it all.

phrases.latin: nunc est bibendum, nunc pede līberō pulsanda tellūs
phrases.english: now we must drink, now beat the ground with free feet

phrases.latin: tantum nivis fodiendum atque ēgerendum fuit
phrases.english: so much snow had to be dug and carried away

phrases.latin: Necesse est maximōrum minima esse initia.
phrases.english: The greatest things must have the smallest beginnings.

phrases.latin: et discās oportet et quod didicistī agendō cōnfirmēs
phrases.english: you must both learn and make sure of what you have learnt by doing it

phrases.latin: puer respondit tacendum esse neque id dīcī licēre
phrases.english: the boy answered that it had to be kept quiet and he was not allowed to tell
